 Advertisement Deputies name suspected bank robber who changed clothes at McDonald's
 Advertisement Updated: 6:57 AM EST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Stephanie Moore Digital Content Manager Deputies name suspected bank robber who changed clothes at McDonald's
 Updated: 6:57 AM EST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Stephanie Moore Digital Content Manager TAYLORS, S.C. — Update:
 Greenville County Sheriff's Office investigators have charged 67-year-old Ricky Andreal Counts with bank robbery, armed robbery, and grand larceny.
 Deputies say they obtained video evidence and a confession from Counts about the suspected bank robbery.
 Advertisement Deputies say they found Counts as he was preparing to board a bus on the 2000 block of Wade Hampton Blvd. They say investigators recovered the stolen money from the bank after finding it in Counts' possession.
 Counts was taken to the Greenville County Detention Center and is being held on $10,000 bond. 
 Update: 
 Suspect in custody. 
 Original story: 
 The Greenville County Sheriff's Office is searching for a suspected bank robber who changed clothes inside a McDonald's. 
 The sheriff's office said the 911 call came into dispatch just before 10:30 a.m. Monday, after a Black man entered the Truist bank, implied he had a weapon and took cash. 
 Greenville County Sheriff’s Office Bank robbery suspect Authorities said the man then left and went to the McDonald's located at 2109 Wade Hampton Blvd. where he changed his clothes. 
 WYFF News 4 Deputies and K-9s are currently tracking the suspect.
 The suspect is described as an older black male with a mustache, wearing jeans, a hooded sweatshirt and no shoes. 
 If anyone has information regarding this incident, they are asked to call 911.
 No injuries were reported.
